subject.title: session.reset: support mode: "never" for manual-only session reset behavior

question: Which public `session.reset.mode` literal and validation semantics should OpenClaw support for manual-only reset behavior?
rationale: This adds a new public configuration value and affects core session lifecycle semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent config contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add `never` mode
options.body: Adopt the reporter's literal for no automatic reset, preserve manual resets, and reject or explicitly ignore daily/idle-only fields in that mode.

options.title: Add `off` or `manual` mode
options.body: Support the same behavior under a different canonical literal that may better match existing OpenClaw config vocabulary.

options.title: Keep workaround only
options.body: Leave `daily | idle` as the only supported modes and document the large-idle workaround, accepting readability and eventual-expiry tradeoffs.

recommendation.title: Add `never` mode
recommendation.body: Adopt the reporter's literal for no automatic reset, preserve manual resets, and reject or explicitly ignore daily/idle-only fields in that mode.

likelyOwner.reason: The original daily reset config/runtime feature traces to this history, making this the best available routing candidate for the public contract choice.
